title: Retention-Intent Evidence Reconciler: automated collector + control->artifact mapping
creator: Maya Patel
description: Build an automated reconciler and collector that maps retention intent (customer-configured retention policies + jurisdictional constraints) to the concrete audit artifacts we store and surface for SOC 2 / ISO 27001 attestations. The feature should produce tamper-evident artifact bundles, include TTL/expiry enforcement, and export deterministic evidence packages for auditors and internal control owners.
acceptance_criteria: Collector can schedule and execute retention-aware snapshots for three different artifact types: access logs, deployment rollout records, and encryption key rotation events
Control->artifact mapping table is stored in a human-readable manifest and can be exported as CSV/JSON for auditors
Reconciler detects missing artifacts for a given control period and produces a remediation report with PR/owner mappings
Bundles are signed (HMAC) and include provenance metadata: region, storage class, TTL, retention policy id
Retention TTL enforcement triggers archival workflows (cold storage) and redaction flows for PII within 48 hours of policy expiration
Automated auditor export endpoint provides a point-in-time bundle for any supported jurisdiction in under 5 minutes for requests up to 10GB

notes: Design decision: use append-only manifest with incremental diffs to minimize re-read of cold storage
Trade-off: full-fidelity retention enforcement vs cost. MVP will redact PII in-situ for expired windows; archive-and-wipe is phase 2
Monitoring: add dashboard panels for "evidence coverage" by control and by region; SLO target 99% reconciled artifacts per control-period
Follow-ups: integrate with Rollouts service to capture canary->prod promotion events as evidence artifacts
Edge case: cross-region failover where primary artifact lived in different jurisdiction — reconciler must surface residency mismatch and suggested remediation
